title: 'Time traveller' claims to be from 3311 and has chilling photo from the future
excerpt: An anonymous man claimed in a ApexTV video to have visited the year 3311, sharing three photos as 'proof'
content:
An anonymous man claimed in a ApexTV video to have visited the year 3311, sharing three photos as 'proof'

08:00, 03 Oct 2026Updated 09:44, 03 Oct 2026

The mystery man claiming to be a time traveller says he has a photo from the year 3311.

‌

‌

The alleged time traveller kept his identity hidden with a blurred face and distorted voice in the footage, yet insisted his account was genuine.

‌

Addressing the camera for the YouTube channel ApexTV, the time traveller presented three photographs he claimed to have captured during a mission to the year 3311. The time traveller said he possessed an "extremely interesting story" to share - a tale concerning both his past and his future.

‌

Putin's scheme to live forever won't work, warp drive is being worked on, archaeologists find the first Paris, and a brilliant banana breakthrough - all this and more in our weird science newsletter

The man said: "What I am telling you is true and I even have the evidence to prove it." He subsequently revealed three photographs depicting what our world allegedly resembles nearly 1,300 years from now.

The initial peculiar image appears to depict a futuristic metropolis constructed on some kind of floating platform suspended in the heavens. The time traveller explained: "This was not the only picture I took in the future.

"I got into the teleportation machine again, but this time it brought me to a very different place, and I took a picture of that place as well. Let me show you that picture."

He then produced a photograph of a structure, which he described as a standard dwelling in the distant future. His final image showed a flying craft soaring above various houses and vegetation.

‌

These three photographs, the time traveller audaciously maintained, were meant to substantiate his dubious narrative.

According to the time traveller, he captured the images after being selected to participate in a classified time-travel mission in the 1990s. He claimed his selection was largely down to his achievements at school in computer development.

‌

And he claimed that the mysteries of time travel had been unlocked through the enigmatic application of quantum computing.

He said: "I can't say the name of that organisation, but I can assure you that organisations like the one I'm describing, and many, many more, not only exist but are carrying out secret programmes behind closed doors."

Nevertheless, all three images provided by the alleged time traveller are skilful manipulations of existing photographs, designed to appear as though they originate from the future.

‌

The first image is a doctored version of a mountain forest valley wallpaper from 7-themes.com, with a hovering metropolis superimposed on it.

The second image is in fact a modified photograph of the Antilia building, which serves as the private residence of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani in South Mumbai, India.

‌

Several viewers who watched the footage saw right through the ruse and exposed ApexTV in the comments section.

YouTube user Mike Mathieu said: "These 'pictures' look about as real as Japanese animation." Vignesh Baidu added: "Next time, at least take a selfie so that we can clarify it's not photoshopped."

And Richard Labeja wrote: "The pictures look fake, especially the floating city. Their perspectives, lighting, and contrast look severely inaccurate."

‌

Is it feasible for humans to journey through time?

Not according to Professor William Hiscock from Montana State University, or at least not in the manner depicted in the ApexTV footage.

The temporal physics expert explained that time-dilation effects permit people to advance through time but not retreat.

He said: "Time travel into the past, which is what people usually mean by time travel, is a much more uncertain proposition.

"There are many solutions to Einstein's equations of General Relativity that allow a person to follow a timeline that would result in her (or him) encountering herself - or her grandmother - at an earlier time.

"The problem is deciding whether these solutions represent situations that could occur in the real universe, or whether they are mere mathematical oddities incompatible with known physics."
